sources.claim: The ticket requires Taurus to generate a generic EFT-compatible json file for browser-based tests.
The ticket requires categorizing Selenium errors into general errors vs. failed assertions.
EFT json generation is opt-in via a new Taurus config flag under modules.blazemeter, default off (option A).
Graceful degradation: empty responseBodies for browser tests and synthetic assertion name when the real name is unrecoverable.
Decision D-1: extract the ERRTYPE_* classification into a shared helper (do not modify JTLErrorsReader).
Decision D-2: generate failed_transactions.json in BlazeMeterUploader.post_process and reuse the existing __upload_artifacts path.
The error_item_skel shape and the DatapointSerializer three-way split are the proven analog to mirror.
Runtime data (FunctionalAggregator.cumulative_results) is available at post_process; assertion-name recovery is a medium-risk VALIDATE item.
Assumption ledger records A-ASSERT as VALIDATE with a POC/contract task.
T008 implements the flag-gated EFT generation hook in blazemeter_reporter.py.
T011 extracts the ERRTYPE_* classification into bzt/modules/eft.py without modifying jmeter.py.
T014 guards the generation path behind the config flag.
T016 implements graceful-degradation handling (empty responseBodies, null rc).
test_artifact_written_when_flag_on covers the artifact-generation requirement.
test_classify_general_vs_assertion covers the categorization requirement.
test_no_artifact_when_flag_off covers the opt-in-default-off requirement.
test_synthetic_assertion_name_fallback and test_empty_response_bodies_and_null_rc cover graceful degradation.
The Constitution Check passes all five principles; the architecture (extract-classify + generate-in-uploader) is resolved.
Negative constraints: do not modify JTLErrorsReader for non-JMeter formats; do not gate EFT in taurus.
T001 creates the realistic Selenium assertion-failure fixture used by the categorization tests.
T007 implements build_failed_transactions mirroring the DatapointSerializer split.
